prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Greenvale Metro: underground/surface; peak/off-peak/engineering-hour. Communications-Based Train Control system (CBTC) protects separation/authority/regulation. Actors: Line Traffic Controller requests safe regulation/recovery; Revenue Train Operator handles readiness/cab/passengers; Cyber Security Officer oversees access/security. Metro Operations Control System (Lantern) sends Crew Login Token Bundle; separately displays commanded/locked routes, points, occupancy, positions/radio/supervision; no vital intervention. Voice Dispatch Console never substitutes safety validation. Passenger Information Gateway distributes approved messages; Service Timetable Server supplies schedules; non-vital outputs isolated.
North District Zone Controller (Marble): northern mainline/turnback/East Junction Interlocking (Falcon) approach. South District Zone Controller (Orchid): southern mainline/turnback/West Junction Interlocking approach. Controllers derive authorities from location/occupancy/field-state; transfer requires ownership/overlap and receiving-zone validation. Interlockings retain point/route locking/release authority. Authorities require detected/locked/proved points, protected overlap/flanks; correspondence loss shortens/withdraws within braking envelope. Boundaries use route/point/vacancy. Restrictive evidence prevails over discrepancies. Axle counters independently prove availability/locking. East sends Axle Counter Reset Request; reset prohibited with locked routes/approaching trains. Maple (full name unspecified) records clearance before restoration. West sends Route Release Exception List; exceptions remain hazards until paths excluded.
Platform Screen Door Controller supplies closed/locked indications, never route proof; absent readiness may hold trains outside berth. Approach protection combines route/stopping supervision.
Atlas Onboard Controller (Kestrel): authenticated/energized/integrity-checked activation; initialization/protected-manual/automatic-train/fallback/cutout; validates authority/context/token; cyclic braking produces Brake Curve Checksum Log. Dual Channel Odometer supplies speed/distance/boundary confirmation; divergence increases uncertainty/separation. Propulsion/braking feedback checked; stale acknowledgements rejected.
Train Radio Modem uses Wayside Radio Access Network (Saffron): monitored overlapping handover, sequence/timeouts; degradation retains validated authority; network sends Radio Handover Audit File periodically. Safety Data Communication Network: deterministic authenticated integrity-protected latency-monitored vital state/acknowledgements; sends Clock Drift Sample Report each synchronization. Maintenance Diagnostic Server records outcomes/timing/detection; no vital decisions.

New part:
S101: The Operations Control Centre workflow begins with the Line Traffic Controller maintaining a live view of train positions, route status, alarms, and service performance across the Greenvale Metro line.
S102: The Metro Operations Control System presents regulating options based on timetable variance, platform dwell time, headway spacing, and the current availability of routes.
S103: The Line Traffic Controller selects holding, skip-stop, turnback, or run-through measures only after checking that passenger impact and downstream recovery have been assessed.
S104: Lantern displays the proposed regulating action, affected train identities, and predicted recovery time before the Line Traffic Controller confirms the command.
S105: The North District Zone Controller applies movement authority constraints according to the confirmed operating state and reports any conflict or unavailable route condition for controller review.
S106: The South District Zone Controller applies the same operating principles for the southern section while preserving separation margins and route locking conditions.
S107: East Junction Interlocking holds the route locked until track section detection, point correspondence, and opposing route conditions meet the configured release criteria.
S108: West Junction Interlocking provides route state indications that allow the Operations Control Centre to distinguish an operational delay from a signalling equipment fault.
S109: When an engineering possession or field report requires a temporary operating constraint, the Line Traffic Controller produces the Temporary Speed Restriction Notice after confirming the limits, speed value, start time, and expected removal condition.
S110: After a temporary operating constraint is active, the Line Traffic Controller monitors actual train performance against the expected delay allowance and adjusts regulation plans when recovery margins are exceeded.
S111: The Atlas Onboard Controller enforces the active movement profile on each equipped train and presents any onboard rejection or degraded mode indication for operational assessment.
S112: The Dual Channel Odometer supports train position confidence by providing independent distance measurement inputs that are considered during degraded operation review.
S113: The Train Radio Modem supports continuous operational messaging, and loss of radio availability is treated as a service risk that may require holding trains before constrained areas.
S114: The Wayside Radio Access Network is monitored for coverage alarms, handover irregularities, and capacity conditions that could affect the stability of train control communications.
S115: The Safety Data Communication Network is monitored as a safety-related bearer, and persistent communication faults are escalated before additional regulating actions are attempted in the affected area.
S116: For incident management, the Line Traffic Controller records the initial event time, train identifier, location, passenger impact, and the first safe operating instruction issued.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
